messages:
support: FYI getting a flood of p95/p99 latency tickets from multiple EU customers complaining about calls to our hosted API timing out when backend routes to APAC. started ~11:02 UTC. ticket refs: #5678 #5681 :exclamation:

mira: seeing the same in dashboard — spike in eu-west1 -> apac egress path. p95 up from 120ms to 1.2s, p99 ~2.4s. traces show extra hops and long TLS handshake times.

sam: @mira can you paste a sample trace? also which POPs affected?

mira: grabbed a failing trace from one customer, pasted below. affected POPs: eu-west-pop2, eu-west-pop4, then hairpin to apac-pop1.

mira: ```
Traceroute to apac-pop1 (203.0.113.45)
 1  10.1.0.1  0.45 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.1 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.2  120 ms
 5  198.51.100.9  130 ms
 6  203.0.113.45  1240 ms
```

jon: that jump at hop 6 aligns with TLS handshake RTT jumps we've been seeing. could be cross-region hairpin or bad upstream route.

net-team-bot: BGP update churn detected: origin AS 64520 announced prepends for certain prefixes at 10:59 UTC; withdraws at 11:07 UTC. Potential route oscillation.

devops: confirmed DNS lookups for model-serving.domain return eu-west-pop4 IPs for some clients and eu-west-pop2 for others — inconsistent anycast mapping. TTLs still 30s.

sam: OK let's triage: 1) repro locally with curl + SNI to mimic client geo. 2) run mtr from both eu-west-pop2 and pop4 to apac-pop1. 3) check TLS handshake details (SNI, session reuse).

mira: repro steps I ran: `curl -v --resolve api.example.com:443:198.51.100.9 https://api.example.com/health` from eu-west-pop4. TLS handshake average 1.1s, server cert exchange delays. Session reuse not happening from some egress paths.

jon: looks like packet path is going eu-pop -> upstream isp -> back to apac via congested path. Could be the prepend causing asymmetric routing. net-team oncall?

net-team-bot: @net-team paging primary oncall (sam) and backup (jon).

sam: I'm on it. I'm seeing per-route ECMP changes in our routers around 11:00 UTC. I'm going to temporarily pin egress for the affected prefixes to eu-west-pop1 to stabilize, then monitor. Rolling change now (canary to 10% traffic first).

infra-bot: Deployment triggered: traffic-pin/eu-west-redirect canary -> 10% at 11:18 UTC by sam.

support: any ETA to customer-facing mitigation? customers asking for updates.

sam: sending short note: "We've detected routing oscillation affecting some EU->APAC paths. We're pinning egress to stable POPs and clearing caches. Expect improvements within 5-10 minutes. We're monitoring p95/p99 and will follow up." :thumbsup:

mira: after canary we see p95 drop from 1.2s to 180ms for canary traffic. good signal.

jon: before we push wider, can we reduce DNS TTL to 10s for the hot prefixes so clients converge quicker if we need to change egress again?

devops: lowering TTL now for api.example.com for affected prefixes. DNS change pushed at 11:25 UTC.

sam: scaling canary to 100% at 11:28 UTC. infra-bot: confirm.

infra-bot: Deployment update: traffic-pin/eu-west-redirect scaled to 100% at 11:28:40 UTC.

mira: p95 back to baseline ~120ms across EU customers at 11:31 UTC. p99 ~260ms. TLS handshake times normalized.

support: customers updated. some asked if this could recur — what's the root cause and permanent fix?

jon: preliminary root cause: upstream BGP prepend and flaps from a transit provider created asymmetric/elevated latency paths. our anycast mapping + low DNS TTL + short-lived BGP changes caused clients to land on POPs whose egress took a bad path to APAC. When provider withdrew the problematic prepends we still had cached mappings and some routers re-ECMP causing oscillation.

sam: mitigation we applied: 1) traffic pin to stable POPs (workaround) 2) lowered DNS TTL to speed convergence 3) engaged transit provider to investigate BGP churn 4) monitoring alert tuned to detect >200ms TLS handshake spikes for eu->apac in next 24h.

net-team-bot: Transit provider case opened: ticket TP-8921, provider investigating route prepends.

devops: follow-up ops task created: review anycast origin health-checks and add protective debounce before switching origins on minor BGP changes.

mira: also adding a TLS session reuse check to our synthetic probes from all POPs to catch handshake regressions earlier.

support: customers on #5678 and #5681 acknowledged update, closing tickets after confirmation.

sam: setting post-incident doc stub in #incidents. will add timeline + mitigations + next steps for durable fix (route dampening, improve upstream SLAs, add origin-debounce).

jon: recommend adding a small startup config change: prefer local POP egress for cross-region calls to reduce hairpin risk unless explicit routing needed. will PR later.

mira: nice work team. keeping watch for next 6 hours. :eyes:

support: thanks everyone, marking resolved for now.

net-team-bot: Monitoring p95/p99 eu->apac: baseline restored. will alert if deviation >20% for 15m.

sam: closing thread in 2h unless we see regressions.
